title: Construction of a TF-miRNA-mRNA Regulatory Network for Diabetic Nephropathy.
authors: Dong, Fuxing; Zheng, Luli; Yang, Guokai
one_liner_zh: 该文基于GEO数据构建糖尿病肾病的TF-miRNA-mRNA调控网络，仅用差异表达与通路分析，无AI或物理模拟方法，TF-DNA互作非核心，仅作网络节点，与本课题关联较弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: This study aims to elucidate the microRNA (miRNA)-messenger RNA (mRNA)-transcription factors (TFs) network relevant to diabetic nephropathy (DN). METHODS: To investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying DN, we conducted an extensive analysis using a Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database, specifically GSE51784, GSE30528, GSE30529 and GSE1009. RNA samples from 66 subjects were analysed to identify differentially expressed mRNAs (DEGs) and microRNAs (DEMs) between individuals with DN and healthy controls. The data underwent preprocessing, followed by Gene Ontology (GO) analysis, Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway analysis and Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) to unveil enriched pathways. Additionally, we constructed protein-protein interaction networks and subnetworks of modules to identify key molecular players. RESULTS: A total of 163 DEMs and 188 DEGs were identified among the four datasets. Furthermore, we identified 37 hub genes with high connectivity and four TFs, namely E1A Binding Protein P300 (EP300), SP100 Nuclear Antigen (SP100), Nuclear Receptor Subfamily 6 Group A Member 1 (NR6A1) and Jun Dimerization Protein 2 (JDP2), which may play crucial roles in the molecular pathogenesis of DN. Additionally, we constructed a co-regulatory network involving miRNAs, mRNAs and TFs, revealing potential involvement of pathways such as the Mitogen-Activated Protein Kinase (MAPK) signalling pathway, phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)-protein kinase B (Akt) signalling pathway and metabolic pathways in the pathogenesis of DN. Finally, using a docking model, we established drug-gene interactions involving key genes in the network, providing potential insights into therapeutic options. CONCLUSIONS: This study explores a gene regulation network of miRNA-mRNA-TFs, identifying potential molecular targets in the aetiology of DN. It also suggests potential targets for genetic counselling and prenatal diagnosis for DN.
abstract_zh: 背景：本研究旨在阐明与糖尿病肾病（DN）相关的微小RNA（miRNA）-信使RNA（mRNA）-转录因子（TFs）网络。方法：为探究DN的分子机制，我们利用基因表达综合（GEO）数据库（具体为GSE51784、GSE30528、GSE30529和GSE1009）进行了广泛分析。对66名受试者的RNA样本进行分析，以识别DN个体与健康对照者之间差异表达的mRNA（DEGs）和微小RNA（DEMs）。数据经过预处理后，进行基因本体（GO）分析、京都基因与基因组百科全书（KEGG）通路分析和基因集富集分析（GSEA），以揭示富集通路。此外，我们构建了蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用网络和模块子网络，以识别关键分子参与者。结果：在四个数据集中共识别出163个DEMs和188个DEGs。进一步，我们确定了37个高连接性的枢纽基因和四个转录因子，即E1A结合蛋白P300（EP300）、SP100核抗原（SP100）、核受体亚家族6组A成员1（NR6A1）和Jun二聚化蛋白2（JDP2），这些可能在DN的分子发病机制中发挥关键作用。此外，我们构建了涉及miRNAs、mRNAs和TFs的共调控网络，揭示了丝裂原活化蛋白激酶（MAPK）信号通路、磷脂酰肌醇3-激酶（PI3K）-蛋白激酶B（Akt）信号通路和代谢通路等可能在DN发病机制中参与。最后，利用对接模型，我们建立了网络中关键基因的药物-基因相互作用，为治疗选择提供了潜在见解。结论：本研究探索了miRNA-mRNA-TFs的基因调控网络，识别了DN病因学中的潜在分子靶点，并为DN的遗传咨询和产前诊断提供了潜在靶点。
